I / me (polite, neutral): I / me (casual, with family and friends)
we / us (includes the person you're talking to)
like that (casual, from "begitu") — very frequent filler
like that / so / in that way
like / such as (casual, replaces "seperti" in speech)
again / more — also "currently" before a verb
until / as far as / to arrive
the one that / which — links a noun to its description
no / not (the everyday spoken form of "tidak")
what's it called (stalling for a word)
right / so — marks the point you've been building to
that / there — points at something, casual
um / whatsit — filler while you search for a word
father — also "sir" to an older man
mother — also "ma'am" to an older woman
older brother — also a term for a male vendor or driver
rotating savings club — members pay in and take turns receiving the pot, as much a social gathering as a financial one
dot / period — said aloud when dictating, or to end an argument
to come along / to join in
to try — also "go on, try it"
